title: A life — content/lives/
description: One file per life. The NN- filename prefix fixes shelf order.

id.description: The permalink — and the portrait's filename: assets/plates/<id>.jpg. Renaming it breaks every `across` link pointing here and orphans the plate.

keep.description: The one line to keep from this life, drawn from the entry's own argument. One sentence that makes sense read alone.

n.description: The person's name as shown: "Mohandas K. Gandhi".

plateless.description: Set this only when the house has decided a life gets the press mark rather than a plate, and say why in one line. `npm run stats` then stops listing it as a gap — a warning that is permanently wrong is how you learn to ignore warnings. Never use it to silence a portrait that simply has not been made yet.

plateOf.x-means: what the plate shows, when it is not a portrait
plateOf.description: Set this only when the plate is an object from the life rather than a likeness — a boat, a manuscript — because no portrait can be used. It replaces "Portrait of …" as the image's description and prints under the plate, on the entry and on its share card, so nobody takes the object for the person. Say what it is, when, and where it is held, from the image's own record: "Submarine B-59 … U.S. Navy photograph — the boat, not the man."

years.description: Lived, shown as 'Lived' in the reader: "1869–1948", "c. 69–30 BC".

group.description: Which shelf filter it sits under: famous, or obscure-but-pivotal.

spineC.description: Livery: the spine colour — a shade darker than `cover`.

ink.description: Livery: the lettering colour on the cover.

motif.description: The pattern pressed into the cover. Anything unrecognised prints as conic.

copy.description: The life, one string per paragraph: the situation, what they actually did, the cost or the part usually left out. Keep each paragraph on one line.

t.description: Exact title. The site turns it into a WorldCat search, so a typo breaks the link.

u.description: Only when the place to start is not a book — an article, an exhibition, an archive. The reader then links it directly and heads the section "Where to start" instead of offering a library search for a book that does not exist.

why.description: Why this book and not the famous one.

corrected.description: The numbers of the colophon corrections that apply to this entry, e.g. [2]. The reader prints them on the entry, so someone reading it learns it was corrected and what changed. Add the number in the same change that runs `npm run correct`.

contested.description: What is disputed about this life, and by whom — the strongest critique, named.
